headline: US Weekly Jobless Claims Rise to 203,000
summary: Initial jobless claims in the US rose to 203,000 for the week ending November 14, exceeding the market forecast of 198,000. Continuing claims also increased by 70,000 to over 1.76 million.
why: Weekly jobless claims are a high-frequency indicator of the US labor market's health, influencing Federal Reserve policy expectations regarding interest rates.

impacts.name: US Labor Market
impacts.why: Higher-than-expected jobless claims suggest a potential cooling in the labor market.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The data exceeded market expectations, signaling a slight softening in labor demand which can influence interest rate outlooks.
